headline: ShallowDefend trains an explicit early decision for multi-turn safety defense
summary: ShallowDefend is a work-in-progress preprint proposing an Assess → Decide → Respond format: on each turn, a model assesses user intent, commits to a parseable safety decision, and generates a response conditioned on that decision. The authors train the decision with either a self-verified reward based on known harmful or benign dialogue labels, or an external judge reward. Across five multi-turn safety benchmarks, the paper reports average safe rates of 90.4% and 93.4% for the self-reward variant on Llama 3.1 8B and Qwen3 8B, respectively; its external-reward variant scores 92.9% and 87.6%. The paper reports that its safety lead holds under six judges. These are author-reported comparisons on two backbones, not independent replication or evidence of deployment-grade safety.
